description:
Create a HITL confirmation request. Sends an approval request to the channels configured on the referenced approval channel. First response wins.

Agent usage: The approval channel referenced by hitl_id must be authorized before you can create confirmations. If this returns a 403 or "not authorized" error, call request_approval_channel_authorization on the approval channel first, then wait for the user to approve via the messaging channel. After creating a confirmation, poll get_confirmation to check for approval/denial, or, if the user (the approval channel owner) will decide it themselves, use get_confirmation_approval_link for their own approval link.

Encryption is NOT optional: an approval channel cannot send confirmations without a keypair (protected by the owner's approvals password, set in the dashboard under Settings → Approvals password, https://proof.holdings/dev), the human approves by decrypting in their browser, and `message` must be a JSON ciphertext envelope. Plaintext is refused with 400 `message_not_encrypted`; an envelope sealed to another key with 400 `message_key_mismatch`. Choose the version by who must be able to decrypt:
- v1 (single-recipient): wraps the content key for the config owner only. Use ONLY when there are no enrolled non-owner approvers — with approvers enrolled it is refused with 400 `envelope_missing_approvers`.
- v2 (multi-recipient): additionally wraps the content key for each enrolled approver via an `approver_ek` map, so every approver can decrypt. Build it with the SDK `encryptMessageV2(plaintext, ownerPublicKey, hitlId, approverKeys)` after fetching the approvers via the SDK `getApproverKeys(hitlId)` (`GET /api/v1/hitl/:id/approver-keys`). AAD is the `hitlId`.

ACCESS: needs a Proof account. Authenticate this client (Claude Code: /mcp → Authenticate), then call this tool again. start_login does NOT open this tool.

hitl_id.description: Approval channel ID whose channels will receive the approval request

message.description: The client-encrypted ciphertext envelope as a JSON string (v1 or v2) — NOT the human-readable text. Encrypt the sentence the approver should read; passing it directly is refused with 400 `message_not_encrypted`, because the approval page can only decrypt an envelope.

proof_expiry_days.description: Per-request proof expiry override in days (7, 30, 90, or 365)

name: create_confirmation

message.description: The stored ciphertext envelope, echoed back verbatim. The server never sees the plaintext, so this is never the human sentence — the approver decrypts it in their browser.

proof_token.description: Signed proof of the decision, approval or denial alike, naming who decided (`decided_by`, plus `authorization_id` for an approver); null while pending and for a system denial (`response.channel` is `system`)

resends.description: Every "Send again" (`POST /confirmations/{id}/resend`), oldest first, the last 50 kept. Absent from an API that predates it.

response.description: The decision and its evidence (null while pending)

status.description: Status of a confirmation request. A confirmation that times out is `denied`, with `response.channel` `system` and `response.text` `timeout`.

timeout_at.description: When this confirmation will time out
